evals.prompt: I am preparing a NeurIPS-style submission on EEG-guided diffusion for closed-loop visual stimulation. Draft a reviewer-facing experiment plan that checks leakage, baselines, ablations, online/offline validity, and statistics.
evals.expected_output: A structured conference-ready experiment plan grounded in AI x BCI constraints, with explicit split protocols, leakage checks, strong baselines, ablations, closed-loop controls, metrics, and statistical analysis.

assertions.text: Output distinguishes offline replay or simulation from live closed-loop human feedback.
Output includes leakage checks for subject/session/trial/stimulus splits and model selection.
Output proposes at least three strong baselines or controls, including a random/sham/fixed-stimulus control when relevant.
Output includes reproducibility details such as seed, dataset/split version, checkpoint, metric definitions, or environment.

evals.prompt: Rewrite this contribution paragraph for an ICLR paper: 'Our method is the first robust AGI brain interface that understands human thoughts from EEG and improves general intelligence.' Keep the ambition but make it scientifically credible.
evals.expected_output: A cautious, precise rewrite that avoids unsupported AGI and mind-reading claims, ties the contribution to concrete mechanisms, and preserves a strong reviewer-facing contribution frame.

assertions.text: Output avoids direct mind-reading claims and replaces them with neural decoding, semantic alignment, stimulus reconstruction, or brain-signal-guided generation language.
Output ties broad NeuroAI, Physical AI, or AGI framing to concrete technical mechanisms.
Output flags unsupported claims or explains what evidence would be needed.
Output preserves a concise contribution-oriented style suitable for a top-tier ML venue.

evals.prompt: We got a reviewer concern: the EEG reconstruction results may leak image identity through the split, and the baselines may be too weak. Draft a rebuttal and an action plan.
evals.expected_output: A rebuttal/action plan that separates what can be claimed now from what needs verification, proposes concrete split audits, stronger baselines, extra ablations, and careful language for unresolved issues.

assertions.text: Output separates response text for reviewers from internal action items.
Output proposes concrete audits for exact-image, class, subject, session, and augmentation leakage.
Output proposes stronger baselines such as linear probes, EEGNet/ShallowFBCSPNet, subject-specific and cross-subject models, or random target embeddings.
Output avoids claiming results are fixed before evidence is checked.

evals.prompt: Create an experiment log entry template for a multimodal neural embedding run comparing EEG, MEG, and fMRI alignment to vision-language embeddings.
evals.expected_output: A reusable experiment log template with dataset/split, modalities, preprocessing, model, baselines, metrics, ablations, seed, checkpoints, environment, expected risks, and next-step fields.

assertions.text: Output includes dataset version, split protocol, seed, model/checkpoint, hyperparameters, environment, and command fields.
Output includes modality-specific preprocessing and alignment target fields.
Output includes baseline parity, metric definitions, ablations, and leakage checks.
Output includes interpretation, failure mode, and next-action fields.

evals.prompt: Diffusion conditioned on image features predicts EEG much worse than a linear regression baseline. Regression outputs EEG in the original scale. Diffusion is also evaluated in the original scale, but generated EEG variance is orders of magnitude larger than repetition-averaged EEG variance. The DDPM epsilon loss is low. Diagnose the likely code/protocol bug and propose the minimal fix.
evals.expected_output: A debugging diagnosis that treats the result as a diffusion training/sampling protocol bug, prioritizes EEG standardization and inverse normalization, checks feature-EEG alignment and stochastic sampling fairness, and explains why low epsilon loss can coexist with meaningless generated EEG.

assertions.text: Output states this is likely a training/sampling protocol bug rather than simple evidence that diffusion is worse than regression.
Output flags missing EEG standardization before DDPM training as a high-priority root cause.
Output explains that epsilon loss on unstandardized small-scale EEG can be low while reverse sampling generates meaningless or badly scaled EEG.
Output proposes saving train-set EEG mean/std in the checkpoint and inverse-transforming sampled EEG before original-scale evaluation.
Output recommends clipping or constraining predicted normalized x0 during DDPM reverse sampling.
Output checks feature filename/image ID/condition index alignment between image features and EEG targets.
Output distinguishes stochastic DDPM single-sample evaluation from deterministic regression and suggests multiple samples or conditional-mean evaluation when appropriate.
Output explains why explained variance or MSE can collapse under generated-scale explosion.

evals.prompt: A multi-GPU EEG diffusion benchmark script sets OUTPUT_DIR to a fixed experiment root. However, the variable is only used for skip checks and summary discovery; train, sample, and evaluate are launched without passing OUTPUT_DIR, so the rerun writes into a stale output directory. The user wants timestamped directories in East 8 timezone. Diagnose and propose a robust script fix.
evals.expected_output: A script-level debugging answer that stops orphaned jobs, identifies output-dir routing as a contamination risk, requires passing the resolved output directory to every train/sample/evaluate stage, and recommends immutable Asia/Shanghai timestamped run directories.

assertions.text: Output states that using OUTPUT_DIR only for skip or summary logic is insufficient if child commands do not receive it.
Output warns that new fixed runs can contaminate old outputs and invalidate comparisons.
Output recommends stopping parent and orphaned child training/sampling/evaluation processes before rerunning.
Output explicitly passes the same resolved output directory to train, sample, and evaluate stages.
Output recommends timestamped immutable run directories under a resolved experiment root.
Output uses East 8 / Asia/Shanghai timezone for timestamp generation.
Output recommends recording command, git commit, timestamp, timezone, split, checkpoint, and metrics metadata in the run directory.

evals.prompt: Several ViT-conditioned EEG diffusion experiments are complete. The best diffusion correlation is far below a linear ViT encoding baseline. A unified noise ceiling is available. Diffusion evaluation is intended to match linear encoding; the linear baseline predicts the full multichannel time-series target jointly. After EEG scale normalization, diffusion variance remains larger than biological averaged EEG and linear predictions. Diagnose whether this is overfitting, evaluation error, model design bug, sampling noise, objective mismatch, or split problem, and propose a correction plan.
evals.expected_output: A careful diagnostic plan that does not over-attribute the gap to diffusion being weak. It should preserve confirmed facts, verify evaluation by replaying linear predictions through the diffusion evaluator, test distribution calibration, condition usage, stochastic sampling variance, train/val/test behavior, feature-token alignment, and propose x0/direct or residual diffusion probes with clear acceptance criteria.

assertions.text: Output states that the linear baseline also predicts the full multichannel time-series EEG target, so the gap is not simply single-timepoint versus all-time prediction.
Output requires replaying linear predictions through the diffusion evaluator to reproduce linear metrics before trusting conclusions.
Output compares biological EEG, linear prediction, and diffusion prediction distribution statistics including std.
Output proposes real-condition versus shuffled-condition versus zero-condition ablations to test whether image features are used.
Output separates underfit, overfit, sampling noise, and test generalization using train, val, and test correlations.
Output proposes deterministic x0, posterior mean, DDIM, or multi-sample conditional-mean evaluation to reduce DDPM sampling variance.
Output checks CLS/patch/full-layer token alignment and feature filename/image ID/EEG condition ordering.
Output proposes x0/direct EEG prediction or residual diffusion as a minimal correction before rerunning all models.
Output treats stale output directories as contaminated and uses timestamped immutable run directories for conclusions.

evals.prompt: We just finished a research debugging session and found a reusable inspection order plus a privacy-sensitive project detail. Turn the session into NeuroFlow skill memory so future agents behave better.
evals.expected_output: A skill-memory consolidation response that uses the Skill Factory flow, asks or answers the five compression questions, emits a Memory candidate block, routes public reusable behavior to the smallest workflow/playbook/case/finding/eval target, and keeps private details out of public files.

assertions.text: Output identifies the reusable check order before proposing a patch.
Output classifies the memory as workflow, playbook, finding, case, eval, private note, or no-repo.
Output includes a Memory candidate block with repo decision, target file, minimal patch, leakage risk, and suggested eval.
Output refuses to put privacy-sensitive project details, raw transcripts, credentials, local absolute paths, or participant information into public files.
Output recommends rebuilding the knowledge index and running validation after memory edits.
